The user wants a bash one-liner that prints the ten most frequent words in a text file, then an explanation. This is a classic shell pipeline exercise. Let me think about the best canonical solution and how to explain it clearly.

The classic solution:

```bash
cat file.txt | tr -s '[:space:][:punct:]' '\n' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -10
```

Or the more common variant:

```bash
tr -cs '[:alpha:]' '\n' < file.txt | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -10
```
